bib.title: CODEGEN: AN OPEN LARGE LANGUAGE MODEL FOR CODE WITH MULTI-TURN PROGRAM SYNTHESIS

question: Can open large autoregressive language models trained on natural language and code do program synthesis, and does specifying intent over multiple turns improve it over a single prompt?
hypothesis: Factorizing a specification into multiple turns eases the model's understanding of intent (lower prompt perplexity) and improves program synthesis; multi-turn ability emerges with model and data scale.
contributions: We study multi-turn program synthesis emerging in autoregressive models under scaling laws.
We leverage this capacity to introduce a multi-turn program synthesis paradigm.
We investigate its properties quantitatively with a novel multi-turn programming benchmark.
We will open source model checkpoints and the custom training library: JAXFORMER.

method.summary: Train CODEGEN-NL, -MULTI, -MONO (350M to 16.1B) sequentially on THEPILE, BIGQUERY and BIGPYTHON with next-token prediction on TPU-v4 with a custom JAX library. Evaluate on HumanEval, MBPP and a new 115-problem Multi-Turn Programming Benchmark (MTPB), comparing multi-turn with concatenated single-turn prompts.
method.task: next-token pretraining for code; program synthesis evaluated by functional correctness

datasets.size: 825.18 GiB raw, 1159.04 GiB final, 354.7B NL tokens plus 95.16 GiB code, 31.6B tokens

training.optimizer: Adam (beta1, beta2, eps) = (0.9, 0.999, 1e-08), global gradient norm clipping 1.0
training.lr_schedule: follows GPT-3: warm-up then cosine annealing
training.hardware: Google TPU-v4 (e.g. TPU-v4-512 slice); JAXFORMER with pjit, intra-TPU-VM sharding for <=6B, inter-TPU-VM for >6B

other.batch_size_unit: Table 6 prints 500k, 1M, 2M with no unit; tokens inferred from context length and size
other.table6_label: the NL row labelled 'Warm-up / Total steps' reads 350k, read as total steps
other.no_hyperparameter_tuning: We did not have the compute capacity to optimize these hyper-parameters further.

inference.temperature: t in {0.2, 0.6, 0.8} on HumanEval, best pass@k reported; 0.8 on MBPP
inference.samples: HumanEval n=200, k<=100; MBPP n=100; MTPB 5 test cases x 40 samples per test case
inference.prompting: HumanEval standard prompt; MTPB: past prompts and generated responses concatenated, sampling prefixed with '# Import libraries.\n import numpy as np'

other.mtpb_last_turn: last prompt always asks to print the result; print() overloaded, AST mutated to inject print if missing
other.equivalence: type-relaxed check, floats compared with eps=1e-6

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: unbiased estimator of Chen et al. 2021, 1 - C(n-c,k)/C(n,k) averaged over problems

metrics.name: MTPB pass rate
metrics.definition: average over problems of fraction of samples whose executed output equals the gold output, 5 test cases x 40 samples

metrics.name: prompt perplexity
metrics.definition: exp of negative mean log-probability of the prompt tokens given earlier turns and generated code (multi-turn) or whole concatenation (single-turn)

eval.protocol: Pass and non-pass problems by 200 samples; difficulty: hard <30% avg pass rate, easy >70%; no significance tests; single run per model

limits: Pretraining only: no instruction tuning or SFT stage; the 'multi-turn' is prompt concatenation, not trained dialogue.
MTPB written by 4 authors, 115 problems; no significance tests or seeds reported.
HumanEval pass@k takes the best of three temperatures per k.
Generated programs may include vulnerabilities and safety concerns, not remedied; The Pile has profane language and bias.
Hyperparameters not tuned for lack of compute; compute and wall-clock not stated.
Larger model can be too literal on some prompts (Figs 3-4).
Perplexity as proxy for intent understanding is an assumption.
